parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Maple Ridge · Websters Corners and Dewdney Trunk Road
MLS® uses Websters Corners as a sub-area name, but the City of Maple Ridge publishes no boundary for it. In the City’s own writing the name is spelled “Webster’s Corners”.

The City’s neighbourhood page says Webster’s Corners is near the border of Maple Ridge and Mission, just off Dewdney Trunk Road, with a network of trails for mountain bikers in the BCIT Woodlot, and that it is an active hub for film production in Maple Ridge.
Webster’s Corners Elementary (25554 Dewdney Trunk Road) and Webster’s Corners Park (25496 Dewdney Trunk Road) are both on Dewdney Trunk Road, which gives a fixed point for the area.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 17, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Maple Ridge and School District 42.
General information only.

Quick facts
Gathered from official sources.
Transit
Route 701’s eastern stop in Maple Ridge is on Dewdney Trunk Road at 248 Street

Route 749, Ruskin / Haney Place, runs as a loop that starts at Haney Place, reaches 280 Street at Lougheed Highway, then comes back. Heading out it follows Dewdney Trunk Road, then 284 Street, then 116 Avenue. The return trip takes Lougheed Highway, then 272 Street, then Dewdney Trunk Road
Timetables

Route 701’s timetable is effective January 1, 2024, and route 749’s is effective June 8, 2026. A TransLink news post dated August 24, 2026 says service improvements on route 701 begin September 7, 2026, so confirm against the current timetable.
Kanaka Creek

TransLink’s 2020 Buzzer post says the nearest bus to Kanaka Creek Regional Park is the 749: get off along Dewdney Trunk Road and walk along 252 Street or 256 Street, which the post says have no sidewalks

Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Websters Corners

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

Official Community Plan Chapter 3 sets the rural designations that cover land outside the Urban Area Boundary. I did not find a City statement that lists Websters Corners by name. Schedule B shows Agricultural, Park, Parks Within the ALR, Forest, Rural Residential, Suburban Residential, Estate Suburban Residential and Conservation uses outside that boundary.

In November 2025 the City adopted updates to its Official Community Plan and to the Albion, Hammond, Silver Valley and Town Centre area plans, it says. Websters Corners has no area plan that I could find.

Outside the Urban Area Boundary, the City’s Official Community Plan sets out three rural residential designations. A Rural Residential lot is typically 0.8 hectares (about 2 acres) with community water available, and 2.0 hectares (about 4.9 acres) if the water is on site. Suburban Residential lots typically run 0.4 hectares (about 1 acre), and so do Estate Suburban Residential lots at 0.4 hectares.

ALR: I did not find an official statement placing Agricultural Land Reserve land inside Websters Corners. ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the Agricultural Land Commission map.
I found no flood designation written for Websters Corners. The City publishes a Be Flood Ready guide and floodplain maps for the Fraser and Alouette Rivers.
Metro Vancouver warns that the cliffs at Cliff Falls in Kanaka Creek Regional Park are steep and slippery.
According to the City, landslides and debris flows are a concern in some parts of Maple Ridge, and warm weather on top of melting snowpacks can trigger landslides.
I found no slope area named for Websters Corners, so check the City’s maps for the exact address.

Websters Corners has no station of its own on the West Coast Express. Maple Ridge has two stops, Port Haney Station and Maple Meadows Station, with five trips daily Monday to Friday, heading out of Maple Ridge each morning and coming back each evening.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Websters Corners

parts.t: Check the OCP designation and zone.
Ask the City which Official Community Plan designation and zone apply to the exact lot, because lot sizes of about 1, 2 and 4.9 acres all appear in the plan.
Check the slope and creek rules.
Ask the City about flood, creek and slope rules for the exact address, especially near Kanaka Creek or a ravine.
Check the water, septic and access.
Find out who supplies the water, request the well and septic records, and see how the property is reached in winter.
Check the ALR and the zone.
Before planning anything on the land, look the address up on the Agricultural Land Commission map, then ask the City what the zoning permits.
Confirm the school catchment.
Ask SD42 for the exact address.
Get a full home inspection.
Check the roof, drainage, furnace, plumbing and wiring, and have the well water tested if there is a well.
Where is Websters Corners?
The City of Maple Ridge has not drawn or published a boundary for Websters Corners, which is a name taken from the MLS® sub-area list. Its own spelling is “Webster’s Corners”.
The City says it is near the border of Maple Ridge and Mission, just off Dewdney Trunk Road.
How do I get around from Websters Corners?
Route 701’s eastern stop in Maple Ridge is on Dewdney Trunk Road at 248 Street.

Haney Place is both ends of route 749, Ruskin / Haney Place, which loops to 280 Street at Lougheed Highway and returns. The outbound leg goes along Dewdney Trunk Road and 284 Street before 116 Avenue, and the inbound leg goes along Lougheed Highway and 272 Street before Dewdney Trunk Road.

Dates on the timetables: 701 from January 1, 2024, and 749 from June 8, 2026. Route 701 is getting better service starting September 7, 2026, according to TransLink’s news post of August 24, 2026, so look at the current timetable before relying on this.

Websters Corners does not have a West Coast Express station. Port Haney Station and Maple Meadows Station are the two stops in Maple Ridge, and the train makes five trips daily, Monday to Friday: out in the morning, back in the evening.
Which schools are in Websters Corners?
Webster’s Corners Elementary, K-7, is at 25554 Dewdney Trunk Road. I found no secondary school in the area; Garibaldi Secondary, Grades 8-12, is at 24789 Dewdney Trunk Road.
Catchments are set by address, so confirm a specific address with
School District 42 (SD42)
What parks and library are there?
Webster’s Corners Park is at 25496 Dewdney Trunk Road, and Kanaka Creek Regional Park, run by Metro Vancouver, is listed by TransLink at 11450 256 Street.
You will find the Maple Ridge Public Library at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road. It is Maple Ridge’s one and only Fraser Valley Regional Library branch.
What plan covers Websters Corners?
I found no area plan for Websters Corners. The Official Community Plan’s rural designations apply to land outside the Urban Area Boundary.
Is Websters Corners in a floodplain or on a slope?
I found no flood or slope statement for Websters Corners in the City’s sources.
Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
What are the homes and lots like?

The Official Community Plan, which is the City’s, names three rural residential designations beyond the Urban Area Boundary. For Rural Residential, the usual lot is 2.0 hectares (about 4.9 acres) on site water, and 0.8 hectares (about 2 acres) once community water is available. The usual Suburban Residential lot is 0.4 hectares (about 1 acre); Estate Suburban Residential is 0.4 hectares as well.
ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the
Agricultural Land Commission map

. Lot size (MLS sales data, not an official source): the median lot size of detached houses sold between July 1 and October 8, 2026 was 55,408 sq ft (about 1.3 acres), based on 7 sales with a recorded lot size.
That is only 7 sales.
